name: Wish list

arrival.name: Match the ad they tapped
arrival.text: Most new users arrive from a Meta ad about stress or anxiety and have never used a meditation app. Speak to the reason they tapped before asking anything personal.
arrival.source: HDYHAU Sep 4: Meta is 40% of respondents at 6.6% trial start vs 13.9% overall; round 2 A2 (newcomers reached a paywall not knowing what the app does)

proof-early.name: Lots of proof before the trial ask
proof-early.text: Awards, ratings, member counts and reviews appear while the user is still deciding whether to give us 3 minutes, not only at the paywall.
proof-early.source: March A3 (the store listing was the strongest pre-app trust signal); Calmer #1; Insight Timer's 5 proof placements

payoff.name: Every question pays off
payoff.text: Each question says why we ask, and the answer visibly changes something within 2 screens.
payoff.source: Growth Gems principle 2; 23-app benchmark rule 2 (reason in the header); rule 3 (result points back to what you said)

echo.name: Say their answers back
echo.text: Read the user's own answers back to them. Personalization the user cannot see is not personalization to them.
echo.source: Synthesis #1 (answer echo, the biggest gap vs the field); round 2 A4 (a named result is where 'it understood me' landed); Alex 5:00 ('a major need')

rhythm.name: Ask, then give back
rhythm.text: The question rhythm: never 2 question blocks in a row. After 1 or 2 questions, pay the user back with a validation, a fact or a look at the product.
rhythm.source: Calmer's spine (15 questions, ~20 interstitials); synthesis #2; round 2: 3 of 4 Calmer testers named the explanations unprompted

sourced.name: Real numbers with a source
sourced.text: Every number carries a source and a date, and results-vary language where it applies. No 'clinically proven', no unsourced stats.
sourced.source: March B4/B5 (age-specific stats were the strongest confidence builder; ours were dated and unsourced); Anna's citation set; Balance whitepaper 2025

felt-value.name: Show the product before the paywall
felt-value.text: The paywall arriving before any sense of the product was the abandonment trigger in March. Previews of real sections and a named first session stand in for felt value.
felt-value.source: March D1 (12 of 18) and F1 (5 of 6 newcomers); round 2 A5 (content access resolved the try-first objection); synthesis #10; paid-UA field read Sep 5 (ReciMe has the user import a real recipe before its paywall)

humans.name: Real coaches, shown not claimed
humans.text: Faces, voices and how the sessions get made answer the 'is this AI' worry without using the word, which plants the thought.
humans.source: Cindy (Sep 2024); coaches prior art; App Store review 'Love that they use real voices and not AI'; 3 competitors sell teacher credibility

reassure.name: A privacy line beside personal questions
reassure.text: A concrete, checkable line next to the field it protects ('never shown to anyone') builds more trust than any general promise.
reassure.source: 23-app benchmark rule 4 (Strava, Gentler Streak: highest trust ratings in the set); the deck had zero reassurance copy

no-deficit.name: No scare copy
no-deficit.text: Validate what the user said, then teach. No presupposed diagnosis, always a 'Not sure'. Calmer's agitate-then-absolve structure is used; its claims are not.
no-deficit.source: Balance voice (compassionate, grounded); synthesis #9; Calmer's dark patterns documented, not copied

commit.name: A small commitment before the trial
commit.text: A realistic practice goal and a reminder time right before the paywall turn intent into a plan, so the trial feels like a decision already half made.
commit.source: Synthesis #4 (Insight Timer's praise ladder, cheapest high-leverage steal); Calmer #41; CYTR +24.7% trial starts

honest-result.name: A profile built only from real answers
honest-result.text: The profile reflects what the user actually said. No invented sub-scores, no manufactured headroom, no clinical framing.
honest-result.source: Round 2 P18 (Calmer scored his healthy diet as Fair and he thanked it); A4; 'not a clinical assessment' line

keep-what-works.name: Keep what already tests well
keep-what-works.text: The goal screens, the reminder flow, the trial-reminder chooser and the live paywall stay as they are. This is a constraint as much as a principle: no first test would remove the goal screens or change the reminder flow, so both versions keep them.
keep-what-works.source: Alex 4:35 ('keep our goal screens as they exist') and Sep 5 ('constraint-driven more than we know this is good'); prior-art census (wins came from reordering and framing, not new content); CYTR and ReciMe are baseline wins

voice.name: Balance voice
voice.text: Accessible, grounded, compassionate, realistic. Digits, full sentences, contractions, no first person except 'Let's', no exclamation points, no 'mindfulness' unless we teach it.

trial-anxiety.name: Say when the trial reminder comes
trial-anxiety.text: Forgetting to cancel is the objection behind the objection. Say when the reminder comes and what happens on day 7 before asking for the trial.
trial-anxiety.source: Round 2 A3 (the trial-reminder paywall was the only element praised unprompted for the objection it targets); Insight Timer and Calmer timelines

description: Calmer's flow in Balance's skin, built as if templates were free. Proof up front, a question rhythm that gives something back after every ask or two, a named profile and a progress graph, then today's paywall.
